The test image shows a tomato plant uprooted at the soil line with:
- White cottony mycelial growth on the lower stem at/near the soil line
- Stem split open revealing discolored internal tissue (yellowish-white pith)
- Completely wilted/dead plant with dried brown leaves
- Crown rot at the soil line

Top candidates: **Southern_Blight** (white mycelium + soil-line crown rot), **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (white cottony mycelium + stem rot), **Verticillium_Wilt** (internal vascular discoloration + wilt).

Now viewing one reference per class across 4 candidates:
Southern_Blight reference: white mycelium on the stem at the soil line, plant pulled up with roots - very similar to the test image.
Sclerotinia reference: wilting above-ground foliage, no white mycelium at soil line - less like the test image.
Verticillium reference: leaf wilting and chlorosis - does not match the stem/crown rot with white mycelium in the test image.

Southern_Bacterial_Wilt reference: shows bacterial streaming diagnostic test in water - completely different from the test image.

**Summary of analysis:**

- **Test image**: Plant uprooted at soil line, white cottony mycelium on lower stem, internal pith discolored/exposed, complete wilt, sandy soil. Classic crown rot presentation.
- **Southern_Blight** reference: near-identical - white mycelium on stem at soil line, plant pulled from ground with roots. Strong match.
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** reference: shows above-ground wilting with no visible white mycelial mat at soil line. Weaker match.
- **Verticillium_Wilt** reference: leaf chlorosis/wilt only, no crown/stem features. No match.
- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt** reference: bacterial streaming diagnostic test. No match.

The white cottony mycelium at the soil line combined with crown rot is the hallmark sign of *Sclerotium rolfsii* (Southern Blight).

This matches the Southern_Blight reference image almost exactly (white mycelium at soil line, crown rot, plant pulled from sandy soil).
